# posthog_endpoint (Resource)

Manage PostHog endpoints. An endpoint turns a HogQL or insight query into a named, versioned API route that callers run with `POST /api/projects/{project_id}/endpoints/{name}/run/`. Changing the query creates a new version, and the endpoint serves the latest one.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Minimal endpoint. Run it with
# POST /api/projects/{project_id}/endpoints/daily-signups/run/
resource "posthog_endpoint" "daily_signups" {
  name        = "daily-signups"
  description = "Signups per day over the last 30 days"

  query_json = jsonencode({
    kind  = "HogQLQuery"
    query = "SELECT toDate(timestamp) AS day, count() AS signups FROM events WHERE event = 'user signed up' AND timestamp >= now() - INTERVAL 30 DAY GROUP BY day ORDER BY day"
  })
}

# Endpoint with a SQL variable. The query names the variable as
# {variables.code_name} and declares it under `variables`, keyed by the
# variable's id. Building both from the posthog_insight_variable resource
# also makes Terraform create the variable first. Callers override the
# default in the run body: {"variables": {"event_name": "$pageview"}}.
resource "posthog_insight_variable" "event_name" {
  name               = "Event name"
  type               = "String"
  default_value_json = jsonencode("$pageview")
}

resource "posthog_endpoint" "event_count" {
  name                   = "event-count"
  data_freshness_seconds = 3600
  tags                   = ["public-api"]

  query_json = jsonencode({
    kind  = "HogQLQuery"
    query = "SELECT count() AS total FROM events WHERE event = {variables.${posthog_insight_variable.event_name.code_name}} AND timestamp >= now() - INTERVAL 7 DAY"
    variables = {
      (posthog_insight_variable.event_name.id) = {
        variableId = posthog_insight_variable.event_name.id
        code_name  = posthog_insight_variable.event_name.code_name
      }
    }
  })
}

# Materialized endpoint. PostHog precomputes the results every
# data_freshness_seconds instead of running the query on each call.
resource "posthog_endpoint" "weekly_active_users" {
  name                   = "weekly-active-users"
  is_materialized        = true
  data_freshness_seconds = 21600

  query_json = jsonencode({
    kind  = "HogQLQuery"
    query = "SELECT count(DISTINCT person_id) AS users FROM events WHERE timestamp >= now() - INTERVAL 7 DAY"
  })
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) URL-safe name, unique in the project. It must start with a letter and hold only letters, digits, hyphens and underscores, up to 128 characters. The name is part of the run URL and PostHog cannot rename an endpoint, so changing it replaces the endpoint.
- `query_json` (String) JSON-encoded query the endpoint runs, for example a `HogQLQuery` or a `TrendsQuery`. Changing it creates a new version in place. A HogQL query references a SQL variable as `{variables.code_name}`; declare it under `variables`, keyed by the `posthog_insight_variable` id, with `variableId` and `code_name`. PostHog fills in values from the variable's default and adds fields of its own, which the provider ignores.

### Optional

- `bucket_overrides` (Map of String) Bucket function per column for materialized range variables, for example `{ timestamp = "hour" }`. Requires `is_materialized = true`. PostHog checks the bucket names.
- `data_freshness_seconds` (Number) How fresh the results must be, in seconds. It sets the cache duration, and the sync interval when the endpoint is materialized. One of `900`, `1800`, `3600`, `21600`, `43200`, `86400` or `604800`. PostHog defaults to `86400`. An organization's plan can set a minimum for materialized endpoints.
- `description` (String) Description of what the endpoint returns.
- `is_active` (Boolean) Whether callers can run the endpoint. Defaults to `true`. Deactivating an endpoint turns off its materialization.
- `is_materialized` (Boolean) Whether PostHog precomputes the results on a schedule set by `data_freshness_seconds`. Defaults to `false`. This reports whether materialization is turned on, not whether the first run has finished. Only active endpoints whose query PostHog can materialize accept `true`.
- `optional_breakdown_properties` (Set of String) Breakdown properties a caller may leave out of a run, for insight queries with a `breakdownFilter`. A run without one returns data aggregated across all its values. By default every breakdown is required.
- `project_id` (String) Project ID (environment) for this resource. Overrides the provider-level project_id.
- `tags` (Set of String) Tags on the endpoint.

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) Timestamp when the endpoint was created.
- `current_version` (Number) Latest version number. It goes up by one each time `query_json` changes.
- `id` (String) The endpoint name. PostHog addresses endpoints by name, so the id and `name` are the same.
- `run_url` (String) Absolute URL that runs the endpoint.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import using: project_id/endpoint_name
terraform import posthog_endpoint.example 12345/daily-signups

# If project_id is configured at the provider level, you can omit it:
terraform import posthog_endpoint.example daily-signups
```
